issues.passage: They planned for vicissitude by freezing every policy for the next decade.
issues.why: "Planned for vicissitude" correctly uses the word for change of circumstances; freezing policy is a paradoxical strategy, not a misuse of the vocabulary.

fix.correctPassage: The firm survived every vicissitude of the volatile market cycle.
wrongPassages: Life under the stable regime was one long vicissitude of unbroken calm.
Investors praised the fund's vicissitude: identical holdings and returns every quarter.
The lake's remarkable vicissitude kept its waterline fixed year after year.

issues.passage: She delivered a lugubrious toast that left the guests laughing for several minutes.
issues.why: A toast can be lugubrious (mournful in tone) and still draw laughter; the word correctly describes the toast's dismal quality.

fix.correctPassage: A lugubrious score made the short documentary feel heavier than its runtime.
wrongPassages: His lugubrious welcome—a bright grin and an easy joke—lifted the mood at once.
The festival stayed lugubrious with brass bands, confetti, and dancing crowds.
She delivered a lugubrious toast full of punchlines that kept the party buoyant.
